digest.headline: Treasury yields surged as US equity indices split and Japanese currency officials discussed exchange rate weakness.

lede.b: US Treasury yields surged past rental returns for the first time in 20 years, pressuring other assets. A bond is a loan you give to a government in exchange for regular interest payments, and its yield is the annual return on that loan. When those yields rise, investing in property or stocks becomes less attractive by comparison. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average headed for its fourth straight weekly loss, while the Nasdaq index hit a high driven by tech shares. Federal Reserve official Schmid questioned if the artificial intelligence ecosystem is becoming too big to fail. Treasury yields top rental returns for the first time in two decades.
lede.i: US Treasury yields extended their surge past rental returns for the first time in 20 years, creating cross-asset pressures. The Dow headed for its fourth consecutive weekly loss, whereas the Nasdaq reached a high led by artificial intelligence infrastructure. Federal Reserve official Schmid questioned whether the AI ecosystem has grown too big to fail. Cable equities traded as the cheapest shares in the S&P 500 while energy stocks gave back their oil premium. Treasury yields top rental returns for the first time in two decades.
lede.a: US Treasury yields extended their surge to top rental returns for the first time in 20 years, compressing valuations across risk assets. The Dow tracks toward its fourth consecutive weekly loss while the Nasdaq diverges to reach a high on artificial intelligence infrastructure outperformance. Federal Reserve official Schmid questioned the systemic scale of the AI ecosystem, asking if it is too big to fail. Cable equities trade as the cheapest segment within the S&P 500 alongside the erosion of the oil premium in energy stocks. Treasury yields top rental returns for the first time in two decades.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: UK banks test tokenised deposits and energy shock concerns

stories.t: Major UK Banks Trial Tokenised Sterling Deposits
stories.b: Barclays, HSBC and Lloyds test digital versions of British money in live transactions. These digital tokens use blockchain technology, which is a shared computer system that records deals securely. This allows large financial institutions to settle payments faster. The trials involve real financial assets moved across digital networks.
stories.i: Barclays, HSBC and Lloyds execute live transactions using tokenised sterling deposits. The institutions test distributed ledger technology to streamline clearing and settlement mechanisms. The commercial bank money representations operate on private networks. These trials mark a shift toward programmable wholesale banking infrastructure.
stories.a: Barclays, HSBC, and Lloyds deploy tokenised commercial bank money in live DLT settlement environments. The initiative tests programmable liquidity management and atomic settlement capabilities across institutional ledgers. Interoperability between disparate private chains remains a key friction point for scaling these digital deposit rails. Settlement finality is achieved without relying on traditional RTGS operating hours.

stories.t: Energy Shock Complicates Bank of England Rate Outlook
stories.b: The Bank of England is the central bank of the United Kingdom, which is the main institution that sets interest rates and manages the national currency. Officials state that an ongoing energy shock may complicate the path for future interest rates. Interest rates act like the cost of renting money. Higher rates make borrowing more expensive for households and businesses.
stories.i: The Bank of England warns that an ongoing energy shock complicates its interest rate path. Monetary policymakers assess how supply-side price pressures impact inflation dynamics. Higher energy costs restrict policy flexibility as officials balance price stability against economic growth. The transmission mechanism relies on adjusting borrowing costs to cool demand.
stories.a: The Bank of England signals that persistent energy shocks complicate the forward guidance and reaction function for policy rates. Exogenous supply shocks complicate the trade-off between anchoring medium-term price stability and accommodating output gaps. Markets reprice terminal rate expectations as monetary authorities weigh second-round price effects against weakening aggregate demand. The transmission channel via energy futures complicates the trajectory of core price indices.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: DAX moves on oil, trade patterns and Rhine levels

stories.t: DAX Reacts to Oil and Peace Hopes
stories.b: The main German stock market index, called the DAX, tracks big companies. Investors watching this index felt more positive. Oil prices dropped, and hopes grew for peace in the war involving Iran. These events helped boost market confidence on September 25, 2026.
stories.i: European stocks rose as declining oil prices lifted market sentiment. The DAX climbed higher on September 25, 2026, supported by renewed hopes for peace in the Iran war. Market experts remained generally cautious despite these daily gains.
stories.a: Equities pushed higher alongside broader European indices as crude prices eased. Sentiment on the DAX found support from diplomatic optimism surrounding the Iran conflict, though technical analysts noted persistent expanding triangle patterns and Elliott Wave projections targeting 24,350 from the August 28 high.

stories.t: Rhine Water Levels Hit New Lows
stories.b: Water levels on the Rhine river dropped to a brand new low. Cargo ships use this river to move goods around. The low water causes transport problems and hurts the German economy. This disruption was reported on September 25, 2026.
stories.i: Rhine river levels reached new lows, creating ongoing transport disruptions. This logistical bottleneck continues to drag on the German economy. The low water constraints were highlighted on September 25, 2026.
stories.a: Rhine gauge readings slumped to fresh lows, exacerbating freight bottlenecks across key industrial corridors. The ongoing logistics friction acts as a persistent macro drag on German economic output. Commercial updates on September 25, 2026 confirmed the severity of the low-water disruption.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Japanese currency discussions and foreign investment reviews

stories.t: Japanese Currency Rallies Following Official Remarks
stories.b: The Japanese yen is a kind of money used in Japan. It gained value against the US dollar after Japanese leaders called the weak currency a problem. Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi called the undervalued currency problematic during talks. Japanese Finance Minister Katayama and US Treasury Secretary Bessent met online to discuss the sliding currency. The currency traded in the mid-157 range against the dollar on the morning of the twenty-fifth.
stories.i: The Japanese yen rallied against the US dollar after political leaders flagged currency weakness as problematic. Prime Minister Takaichi described the undervalued exchange rate as an issue during recent remarks. Finance Minister Katayama conferred with US Treasury Secretary Bessent via an online meeting to address the depreciation trend. The currency subsequently hovered in the mid-157 range against the greenback.
stories.a: The Japanese yen appreciated against the US dollar following explicit policy signaling regarding currency undervaluation from Prime Minister Takaichi. Bilateral coordination intensified as Finance Minister Katayama engaged US Treasury Secretary Bessent in an online consultation concerning persistent FX depreciation dynamics. Spot exchange rates reacted immediately, testing the mid-157 range against the dollar.

stories.t: Japan Modernizes Foreign Investment Screening Filings
stories.b: Japan plans to move its foreign investment review filings online. The system works like the CFIUS process in the United States. Officials announced the digital shift to handle review documents more efficiently. Companies submitting foreign investment applications will use the new web portal.
stories.i: Japan transitions its CFIUS-style foreign investment review filings to an online format. Authorities designed the digital platform to streamline administrative burdens for inbound capital applications. Regulators will process cross-border corporate filings through the updated web infrastructure.
stories.a: Japan digitizes its CFIUS-style foreign investment screening framework by migrating filing procedures online. The administrative overhaul aims to optimize throughput for inbound M&A scrutiny and national security reviews. Compliance mandates require submitting cross-border transactional disclosures through the newly established web portal.

politics.b: Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi spoke about the problems of a weak currency. Finance Minister Katayama met with US Treasury Secretary Bessent to talk about currency trends.
politics.i: Prime Minister Takaichi addressed currency valuation concerns publicly. Finance Minister Katayama coordinated with US Treasury Secretary Bessent in bilateral talks regarding exchange rate trajectories.
politics.a: Prime Minister Takaichi highlighted currency undervaluation risks, aligning with recent summit concerns raised by President Trump. Finance Minister Katayama operationalized these diplomatic pressures through direct bilateral consultations with US Treasury Secretary Bessent.

timeline: Finance Minister Katayama and US Treasury Secretary Bessent held an online meeting to discuss yen depreciation.

stories.b: Eswin Computing wants to sell shares to the public in Hong Kong. This is called an initial public offering, which is how a private company becomes public. The chipmaker aims to raise 300 million dollars. Sources shared these details with reporters.

stories.b: Qingxing raised almost 100 million yuan. The company builds quantum-inspired artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence helps computers think and learn like humans. This money will help them build their new technology.
stories.i: Qingxing secured nearly 100 million yuan in a new funding round. The firm develops quantum-inspired artificial intelligence. The capital injection supports ongoing technology research and development.

stories.t: BYD Schedules Da Han Sedan Release
stories.b: BYD will release its Da Han sedan on October 13. The electric vehicle can travel up to 1,008 kilometres on a single charge. Electric vehicles run on battery power instead of petrol. Drivers can go very far before needing to plug in.

stories.a: BYD slated its Da Han sedan commercial introduction for October 13. The vehicle features a maximum electric range of 1,008 kilometres. The specifications target extended-range consumer demand within the domestic automotive market.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI auctions, state debt and falling foreign reserves

stories.t: Central Bank Announces Liquidity Auction and Treasury Bill Calendars
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India, which is the country's central financial institution managing money and banking, will hold an overnight variable rate reverse repo auction for ₹2,00,000 crore on September 28, 2026. This process allows the central bank to absorb extra cash from the banking system for one day. The Reserve Bank of India also published a treasury bill issuance calendar totalling ₹24,000 crore for auction on September 30, 2026. State governments plan to raise ₹22,200 crore by selling stock through auctions. The central bank set the ways and means advances limit at ₹50,000 crore for the second half of the financial year.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India announced a variable rate reverse repo auction of ₹2,00,000 crore for September 28, 2026, targeting short-term liquidity management. The institution simultaneously scheduled ₹24,000 crore of treasury bill auctions for September 30, 2026, alongside a separate calendar for marketable dated securities. State governments offered stocks worth ₹22,200 crore via public auctions. Furthermore, the central bank fixed the ways and means advances limit at ₹50,000 crore for the period from October 2026 to March 2027.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a variable rate reverse repo operation for ₹2,00,000 crore with a one-day tenor to drain surplus liquidity from the interbank market. Concurrently, the issuance calendar for 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day treasury bills outlines ₹24,000 crore of paper for the auction dated September 30, 2026. State governments collectively brought ₹22,200 crore of state development loans to market across multiple tenors. The ways and means advances ceiling was established at ₹50,000 crore for the second half of fiscal year 2026-2027, with fresh market loan floatation triggered at 75% utilization.

stories.t: Equities Extend Losses as Foreign Investors Sell and Reserves Drop
stories.b: Stock market indexes like the Sensex and the Nifty finished higher on September 25, 2026, because crude oil prices eased and hopes for a US-Iran pact improved market sentiment. Despite this daily gain, the Nifty index finished its seventh straight week lower, which is the longest losing streak since the year 2020. Foreign institutional investors sold ₹11,490 crore worth of shares over a five-day period. India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $14.9 billion, marking the sharpest weekly drop since November 2024.
stories.i: The Sensex and the Nifty closed higher on September 25, 2026, driven by softer crude prices and geopolitical sentiment regarding a US-Iran pact. Nevertheless, the Nifty concluded its seventh consecutive weekly decline, matching its longest losing streak since 2020. Foreign institutional investors offloaded ₹11,490 crore in equities over five trading days. Foreign exchange reserves contracted by $14.9 billion, representing the sharpest weekly contraction since November 2024.
stories.a: Domestic indices recovered ground on September 25, 2026, as falling crude prices and optimism over a US-Iran pact supported risk appetite. Despite this single-session rebound, the Nifty sealed a seventh consecutive weekly loss, mirroring the duration of the 2020 drawdown. Foreign institutional investors liquidated ₹11,490 crore of domestic equities across five sessions. Foreign exchange reserves registered a $14.9 billion drawdown, hitting the steepest weekly decline since November 2024.

politics.b: The Reserve Bank of India reported that state government liabilities and assets data showed loans to state governments stood at ₹19,427 crore as of September 18, 2026. Foreign exchange reserves data was updated alongside weekly statistical supplements. Money supply data was published for the fortnight ending September 15, 2026.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India published its weekly statistical supplement detailing central and state government accounts. Loans and advances to state governments reached ₹19,427 crore on September 18, 2026. Money supply figures for the fortnight ended September 15, 2026, were officially released.
politics.a: The Reserve Bank of India released the weekly statistical supplement detailing central and state liabilities. State government loans and advances registered at ₹19,427 crore for the week ended September 18, 2026. Money supply statistics for the fortnight concluded on September 15, 2026, were simultaneously disclosed.

stories.t: Brazil Inflation Surpasses Forecasts
stories.b: Inflation means that prices for everyday items go up over time. In Brazil, inflation has beaten expert forecasts. This comes as rising United States Treasury yields weigh down Latin American assets. Latin American assets are investments tied to countries in Central and South America.
stories.i: Brazil inflation exceeds forecasts as rising United States Treasury yields weigh on Latin American assets. Regional investments head for weekly losses following the data release. Price growth in Brazil surprises analysts who predicted lower figures.
stories.a: Brazil inflation prints exceed consensus, compounding regional asset losses driven by rising United States Treasury yields. Latin American equities and currencies face weekly drawdowns as higher global discount rates compress valuations. Local price dynamics decouple further from central bank targets.

stories.b: SLB won four contracts from Saudi Aramco to build more than 450 wells. SLB is a large company that provides oilfield services. This work helps expand its presence in Saudi Arabia. Aramco is the state-owned oil giant of the country.
stories.i: SLB secured four contracts from Saudi Aramco to construct over 450 wells. The agreement expands the oilfield services provider's operational footprint in Saudi Arabia. Aramco awarded these projects to maintain its well development pipeline.
stories.a: SLB captured four construction contracts encompassing over 450 wells from Saudi Aramco. The deployment deepens the service provider's regional footprint within Saudi Arabia's upstream sector. The award accelerates Aramco's well construction velocity.

stories.b: Saudi Aramco restored the East-West pipeline after war risks closed in on Yanbu. Houthi forces claimed attacks on Riyadh and the Aramco facility in Yanbu. French troops will protect the Yanbu facilities from the Houthis.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco restored the East-West pipeline as war risks approached Yanbu. Houthi attacks targeted Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu. French troops are set to protect these Yanbu sites from further Houthi strikes.

stories.b: An initial public offering is when a private company sells shares to the public for the first time. Investors rushed to buy shares in the Dangote Refinery. Billions of naira poured into the offering minutes after it opened. The rush showed massive demand for the new stock.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Higher rates and oil depress prices as currency retreats

stories.t: Australian Dollar Retreats on Interest Rate Pressures and Currency Trade Unwinding
stories.b: The Australian dollar dropped after investors unwound a popular trading strategy known as a carry trade, where traders borrow low-interest money to buy higher-yielding assets. Higher interest rates and oil costs pushed share prices lower across the market in what analysts call a September swoon. The Australian dollar rebounded slightly from 0.7000 after the US dollar eased following a strong week.
stories.i: The Australian currency underperformed as traders dismantled a carry trade strategy amid broader market weakness. Higher rates and oil prices depressed equity valuations during the ongoing September swoon. The exchange rate later bounced back from 0.7000 against the US dollar following the American currency's retreat.
stories.a: The carry unwind pressured the Australian dollar alongside falling equity valuations driven by rising commodity and borrowing costs. Higher oil prices and interest rate expectations amplified the September swoon across domestic indices. The pair recovered toward 0.6970 and 0.7000 as the US dollar relinquished gains from the prior week.
